name: Pediatric clinical records (encounters and observations of minors)
rationale: State rules retain minors' records to age of majority plus limitation period; one cited state keeps them until age 30 [VERIFY]. Clinics reach the server over the public internet via HTTPS.

name: Adult clinical records (encounters orders and observations)
rationale: Adult clinical retention typically 5-10 years after last service [VERIFY].

name: Highly sensitive categories (HIV status; mental health; genetic)
rationale: Confidentiality is effectively lifelong; capped at 30y because the CRQC model is extrapolated beyond that.

name: Patient identifiers and demographics
rationale: Identity persists for the patient's lifetime; frequently scraped or enumerated.

name: User credentials and session tokens
rationale: Session lifetime in hours. Control case: the quantum leg must vanish.

name: Lab and referral results exchanged with external systems (HL7/FHIR)
rationale: New results arrive continuously; every record crosses an organisational boundary.

name: Concept dictionary and metadata (published terminology)
evidence_for_zeroing: Terminology dictionaries are published openly; no confidentiality requirement.
rationale: Control case: both legs must vanish.

name: Off-site backups and replicas of the clinical database
rationale: Long-retention copies replicated over partly exposed paths; rarely attacked directly.

name: Application to database link inside the data centre
rationale: MySQL connections are unencrypted unless configured [VERIFY]. No quantum-vulnerable key exchange to attack.

name: Facility-to-facility patient data transfer
rationale: Documented as TLS with mutual certificate authentication between clinics [VERIFY]; crosses the internet.
